Q: How can I make hidden supplementary content available to assistive technologies and mobile users? A:

I've updated my question with some basic examples of how the title attributes are used.

As I detailed in my question, the tooltips aren't a user-friendly option for mobile or AT but switching them to aria-label doesn't solve the problem as it would hide the info from both desktop and mobile users. It also leads to the issue I mentioned of "Data sourced from…" being repeated over and over again when included with the content itself. It gets grating with VoiceOver for sure.

I'm trying to find a solution that works for all 3 situations, either a single solution or a combination of options so the info is available to all users regardless of device or accessibility level. And in a way that separates the content from the supplemental content.

Perhaps this is impossible to do without some advanced JS or maybe this just isn't the approach to take. The project brief does not allow this supplemental content to be listed in the UI itself. So I may need to revisit this with the client to find an accessible option for all.

Q: mysql data-cleaning string-matching normalization A:

Data cleanup is always tedious, inefficient, thankless, and requires some manual work to handle the last few cases.

Another trick for pattern-matching is to use MySQL's SOUNDEX() function.

UPDATE olist_geolocation_staging_2 
SET geolocation_city = 'sao paulo'
WHERE SOUNDEX(geolocation_city) = SOUNDEX('São Paulo');

But there's no solution to correct 100% of the variations.

The best you can do is what you're doing, using several different methods that hope to correct some of the variations. Once you do a few of these methods, you'll fix the majority of them.

But no matter how many pattern-matching solutions you use, you can't know that you've fixed all of them.

So you must do a final scan. I'd do the following query after making a few attempts like you're doing:

SELECT DISTINCT geolocation_city
FROM olist_geolocation_staging_2
GROUP BY geolocation_city;

This will show you the list of distinct cities, some of which will still be misspellings that you need to correct manually. But there will be fewer that need manual updates.
